text:
Aisha: Heads-up — p99 TTFT spike in ap-south-1 since ~03:10 UTC, tokens/sec dropped ~40%. Grafana alert fired, throwing a bunch of noisy buckets. Anyone oncall?
ops-bot: Alert: TTFT_p99_region{region=\"ap-south-1\"} > 1200ms (fired) — group: inference-token-slo — alert_id: 9832
 mike: I'll grab traces. First glance shows tailqueueing on a subset of pods, but the token distribution looks normal. Rolling up by model_family shows most of the traffic on gpt-medium variants.
 sasha: Can you paste the prom query you used? want to reproduce locally.
 mike: Query I used in Grafana panel (5m range):
 ```
 histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster, region, model_family))
 ```
 mike: If you roll up by cluster the spike is localized to cluster-ap-south-1a.
 kevin: Is it CPU or GPU bottleneck? node exporter and nvidia-smi?
 mike: node-exporter shows high irq/softirq on a couple of nodes (nic interrupts). nvidia-smi looks healthy.
 sasha: That smells like noisy NIC or driver flapping — we saw a similar pattern last quarter when a kernel update changed IRQ affinity.
 Aisha: ops-bot also logged a bunch of retransmits around the same time. Could be network path degradation to that AZ.
 ops-bot: NetworkEvent: interface=eth0, node=node-az1-07, rx_errors=120, tx_errors=0, retransmits=43 — recorded 03:07-03:12 UTC
 mike: I'm ssh-ing into node-az1-07 now, collecting dmesg + ethtool stats.
 mike: quick snapshot:
 ```
 # ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_
 tx_packets: 12345678
 tx_errors: 0
 tx_dropped: 30
 # dmesg | tail -n 40
 [ 1200.123456] ixgbe 0000:00:04.0: Reset adapter due to link event
 ```
 sasha: OK that matches driver-level link resets. For short-term mitigation we should: 1) widen alert window to reduce noise (current 1m eval). 2) add a region rollup panel so we can see rollups across AZs. 3) trigger a graceful reschedule for pods on nodes with link-reset flaps.
 kevin: Agreed. I'll open a tiny alert tweak PR to change eval to 5m and add a 'noisy-node' label suppression for 15m. PR sketch: https://github.com/redwood/inference/ops-alerts/pull/472
 Aisha: Please include something to aggregate tokens/sec by model_family and host to detect noisy shards early. Current panel hides host-level spikes.
 mike: Proposed tokens/sec query to add as a drilldown:
 ```
 sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[2m])) by (host, region, model_family)
 ```
 sasha: Also suggest adding a derived p95/p99 breakouts by request_path where possible — some clients hit long prefixes.
 Aisha: Action items:
 - kevin: PR to change alert eval to 5m + transient suppression (PR link above).
 - mike: cordon node-az1-07 and drain pods to test whether p99 subsides.
 - sasha: add a Grafana rollup panel (region -> AZ -> host) and add host drilldown link in token-slo dashboard.
 - ops: follow up with cloud networking to check link flaps / NIC firmware for node-az1-07.
 kevin: Done the PR draft, added note about not muting ondedicated-sla queues. cc @Aisha.
 mike: cordoned node and started drain (kubectl drain node-az1-07 --ignore-daemonsets). Observing tokens/sec on the cluster now — p99 trending down after pods reschedule.
 deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback-sidecars-2026-03-12 — target: cluster-ap-south-1a (triggered by mike)
 sasha: After drain, p99 dropped from ~1.5s to ~380ms on affected cluster, tokens/sec recovered to ~95% of baseline. Looks like noisy NIC was the culprit.
 Aisha: Nice. For permanent fix: schedule firmware update and consider node replacement policy for nodes with >3 link resets in 24h.
 kevin: I'll draft the runbook entry and add a Grafana annotation when we saw the mitigation (so future runbooks match the chart). PR for runbook: https://github.com/redwood/inference/runbooks/pull/99
 mike: leaving this thread; I'll add pod logs + node-exporter snapshots to the incident ticket (INC-2026-314).
 Aisha: Closing loop — thanks y'all. I'll update the token-slo dashboard with host drilldown and rollup change tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
